Each row is classified right only when the dialect arrives: with no
    dialect, a data query naming another engine's catalog would be hidden
    too, and a ``#``-led ``SHOW`` would read as a data query and be shown.
verify_against: src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py is_introspection_query (None-dialect fallback union and SHOW detection)
verify_hint: Trace `is_introspection_query("# note\nSHOW TABLES", dialect=None)` and `is_introspection_query("SELECT id FROM sqlite_widgets", dialect=None)`; a None-dialect result of introspection for the first, or data for the second, falsifies it. Also note the first row's data query relies on the SQLite fallback-union entry (criterion 1/6).
evidence: Docstring at tests/unit/test_query_database.py:1164-1166. Row 1 (mysql URL, data_sql 'SELECT id FROM sqlite_widgets'): readonly.py _catalog_names (212-217) with dialect None returns _ALL_CATALOG_SCHEMAS/_ALL_CATALOG_NAME_PREFIXES, the union, which includes the sqlite entry ('sqlite_','pragma_') from _CATALOGS_BY_DIALECT (200-209); is_catalog_table (320-333) then does name.lower().startswith(prefixes) so 'sqlite_widgets' is a catalog table and is_introspection_query(dialect=None) returns True (hidden). Under dialect 'mysql', prefixes is () and schemas are only information_schema/mysql/sys/performance_schema, so it is data (shown). Row 2 ('# note\nSHOW TABLES'): under mysql, the MySQL tokenizer treats '#' as a line comment so first_sql_keyword returns 'SHOW' (254-293 returns True before parse). With None dialect, sqlglot's base Tokenizer has COMMENTS = ['--', ('/*','*/')] (sqlglot/tokens.py:563) and maps '#' to TokenType.HASH (tokens.py:156), so first_sql_keyword returns '' (non-word first token, readonly.py:160-163), the SHOW shortcut is skipped, and the text then either fails to parse (ParseError/TokenError caught, returns False at 296-303) or yields no catalog Table; in either case the result is False (data query, shown). I could not execute the code (no shell), so the None-dialect parse of the '#' text is traced from the tokenizer source, and the result is False on every branch. Both halves of the docstring hold. The other-engine-catalog row is the SQLite fallback-union entry, as the hint notes.

claim: Changed test lines stay within the repo's ruff line length of 100 (e.g. the BOM byte-string at test_config_smoke.py:131 and the TOML strings at test_local_config_security.py:110 and :132).
verify_against: pyproject.toml [tool.ruff] line-length and per-file ignores; AGENTS.md Code style

evidence: pyproject.toml:96-110 sets [tool.ruff] line-length = 100 and lint select includes E (E501 active), with no tests/ exemption (AGENTS.md.src:114 matches). test_config_smoke.py:131 (the BOM byte-string) is not matched by a regex .{101,}, so it is within 100. Lines tests/unit/test_local_config_security.py:110 and :132 do exceed 100 raw characters (the dispute is right about that). They are still not E501 violations. Ruff's E501 skips an overlong line whose last whitespace-separated chunk contains '://' and starts before the limit, and skips a line that is a single whitespace-free word. Line 110's last chunk is `'[database]\nurl="mysql+pymysql://u@db.invalid/shop"\n')`, which contains '://' and starts around column 50. Line 132 is one whitespace-free string literal after indentation and also contains '://'. Both are therefore exempt, so the claim that the changed lines stay within the repo's enforced ruff line length holds. Caveat: I had no shell, so I did not run `ruff check --select E501`. This rests on my reading of ruff's documented E501 URL and single-word exemptions. The claim's '100' is literally false for raw character count on :110 and :132, but the claim is about what the ruff limit permits.

evidence: Base view tests/unit/test_safety_whole_row.py:49 has DIALECTS = ["mysql", "sqlite", None]; the diff (diff.patch ~3299-3303) changes only that line to ["mysql", None] in this file. Tests using DIALECTS in base: test_refused_shapes (:132-137), test_allowed_shapes (:140-143), test_table_statement_is_refused (:190-206), test_empty_statement_is_refused_as_unsafe (:258-263). Each has one dialect-independent expected outcome (the same pytest.raises class or star text for every dialect), so a sqlite row can never expect something different from the mysql row. The only dialect-dependent logic in the guard is is_catalog_table (readonly.py:320-333, _CATALOGS_BY_DIALECT at :200-203): sqlite adds only the sqlite_ and pragma_ prefixes. None of the SQL in REFUSED/ALLOWED/TABLE/empty-statement lists (:52-129, :194-199, :259) references sqlite_*/pragma_*. The only catalog they use is information_schema (:99, :121), which is in _SHARED_CATALOG_SCHEMAS (readonly.py:198) and counts under every dialect. The genuinely SQLite-specific cases (sqlite_master, pragma_table_info, base :153-154) live in test_allowed_dialect_specific_shapes, which is not parametrized over DIALECTS and is untouched by the diff. One parse nuance: the quoted 'SELECT "table" FROM t' cases (:126-127) parse as an identifier under sqlite but as a string under mysql; the None dialect (default sqlglot, double-quote identifier) still covers that path and the outcome (allowed) is the same. Not run: I did not execute the tests; the same-outcome conclusion rests on the single shared assertion per test and the code reading above.

claim: Every test parametrized over DIALECTS in test_safety_table_shorthand.py gave `uses_table_shorthand` the same expected outcome under `sqlite` as under `mysql`, so removing `sqlite` drops only duplicate cases.
verify_against: base view tests/unit/test_safety_table_shorthand.py and `uses_table_shorthand` in src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py
verify_hint: Compare each DIALECTS-parametrized test in the base view's test_safety_table_shorthand.py against `uses_table_shorthand` in readonly.py for any sqlite-keyed branch or sqlite-only tokenization difference
evidence: Base tests/unit/test_safety_table_shorthand.py:15 has DIALECTS=['mysql','sqlite',None]; head line 15 is ['mysql', None]. The two parametrized tests (test_table_shorthand_is_found, test_other_sql_is_not_flagged) assert one fixed outcome per sql string for every dialect, so expected outcomes are identical across sqlite and mysql by construction. uses_table_shorthand (src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:79-121) has no sqlite-keyed branch: it only calls Dialect.get_or_raise(dialect).tokenize(sql) and scans for TokenType.TABLE tokens, with previous-token text (case-folded) checked against _TABLE_KEYWORD_NOT_SHORTHAND_AFTER, and quoted IDENTIFIER/STRING tokens resetting previous. I also compared the installed sqlglot tokenizers (.venv sqlglot/dialects/sqlite.py:32-54, mysql.py:87-101, tokens.py:404,533-547) against each case. 'TABLE' is a base keyword in both with no override. sqlite differs from mysql only by double-quote identifiers vs strings, '[..]' identifiers, hex strings, MATCH/ATTACH/REPLACE-as-command. Double-quoted cases ('SELECT "table" FROM t', 'FROM "table"', 'FROM "create" TABLE users') are IDENTIFIER under sqlite and STRING under mysql, but both count as quoted, so the outcomes are the same. EXPLAIN is a COMMAND under sqlite, so the rest is swallowed into a string token, and a DESCRIBE token under mysql, where previous='EXPLAIN' exempts TABLE; both give not-flagged. SHOW is swallowed as a command in both. The None dialect still covers the base double-quote-identifier tokenization. No case has a sqlite-specific outcome, so dropping sqlite removes only duplicate cases. The installed sqlglot is the .venv copy in the issue-381 worktree, not a supplied dependency_sources directory, and I did not run the tests.

claim: The system prompt's Tool Errors bullets and Data Confidentiality section are the same for the `sqlite` dialect as for `mysql`, so removing the `sqlite` parametrize case drops only a duplicate.
verify_hint: Check the per-dialect table in `DefaultSystemPromptBuilder` (src/sqllens/agent/ system prompt builder) for any sqlite-keyed text affecting the Tool Errors and Data Confidentiality sections; also see `test_data_confidentiality_declines_whole_table_exports` in test_system_prompt.py
evidence: In src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py the Tool Errors bullets (lines 216-221) are static strings. The only variable is rule_set_error_rule, which depends on self.rule_sets and not on dialect. The tests build the prompt with no rule sets, so their four asserted bullets (_TOOL_ERRORS_BULLETS, test_system_prompt.py:461-473) are identical for sqlite and mysql. The first Data Confidentiality bullet (default.py:224), the one test_data_confidentiality_declines_whole_table_exports asserts as section[0] (test_system_prompt.py:681-690), is a static string with no dialect input. Removing the sqlite parametrize case from both tests (base had mysql, sqlite, None; head has mysql, None) therefore drops only duplicate coverage. Caveat: the Data Confidentiality section as a whole is not identical across dialects. Bullet 3 (default.py:226) interpolates introspection_how, which uses _CATALOG_EXAMPLES (default.py:24-27): sqlite gives '(e.g. sqlite_master)' and mysql gives '(e.g. information_schema.columns)'. Neither removed test asserts that bullet. The sqlite catalog example is still asserted by test_database_section_names_the_engine, which keeps its sqlite case (test_system_prompt.py:430, 449). So the claim's conclusion holds for what the removed cases asserted, but its wording 'Data Confidentiality section' overstates sameness.
